title: Running Commentary on Torah 42 — Va'Yar Ba'Tzar Lahem
hebrewTitle: פירוש רץ על תורה 42 — וירא בצר להם
author: Pettek Nanach
methodology: Three-layer line-by-line gloss: beginner = readable English prose with bracketed translations; intermediate = compact bilingual summary with citations; scholarly = terse Hebrew citation list. Coarse 4-segment structure preserves Rabbeinu's own ois-marking; each segment unfolds the full content of all aligned_segments within its span.

segments.beginner: The verse 'For I, Hashem, am your healer' (Exodus 15:26) hints at the answer 'Amen, may it be His will' through its initial letters: Amen-Ken-Yehi-Ratzon. Healing flows precisely through this affirming response after blessing or prayer. To say 'Amen ken yehi ratzon' is to draw down the divine healing embedded in the verse itself.
segments.intermediate: **"כִּי אֲנִי יְהוָה רֹפְאֶךָ"** (שמות טו:כו) — ראשי תיבות: **אָמֵן כֵּן יְהִי רָצוֹן**. Refuah is drawn through the affirmation 'Amen ken yehi ratzon' — its rashei-teivos are encoded in the very name of the Healer. (See elsewhere — likely Likutey Halakhos and Likutey Moharan I, Torah 60 on amen.)
segments.scholarly: [T2:42] רת"ש "כי אני ה' רפאך" — אכי"ר. עי' לק"ה ברכת הלל; לק"מ ח"א ס' ס' בעניין אמן.
